blurb.K-2: Find out what is inside a big computer building.
blurb.3-5: Build one in Wilmington and see what it needs to run.
blurb.6-8: Build one in Wilmington and measure what it uses.
blurb.9-12: Build one in Wilmington and size up its power demand.

goal.K-2: Students say what a data center is (a building full of computers) and name two things it needs: electricity, and water to stay cool.
goal.3-5: Students explain what a data center does, why it needs a lot of electricity and cooling, and compare its electricity use to homes.
goal.6-8: Students describe how a data center turns electricity into computing and heat, estimate its electricity use in home-equivalents, and name trade-offs for a town.
goal.9-12: Students convert a data center's power (MW) into yearly energy (MWh) and home-equivalents, explain why cooling uses water, and weigh local costs and benefits.

K-2: K-ESS3-3: Communicate solutions that will reduce the impact of humans on the land, water, air, and/or other living things in the local environment.
K-2-ETS1-1: Ask questions, make observations, and gather information about a situation people want to change.
3-5: 4-PS3-2: Make observations to provide evidence that energy can be transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat, and electric currents.
5-ESS3-1: Obtain and combine information about ways individual communities use science ideas to protect the Earth's resources and environment.
6-8: MS-ESS3-3: Apply scientific principles to design a method for monitoring and minimizing a human impact on the environment.
MS-ESS3-4: Construct an argument supported by evidence for how increases in human population and per-capita consumption of natural resources impact Earth's systems.
9-12: HS-ESS3-4: Evaluate or refine a technological solution that reduces impacts of human activities on natural systems.
HS-ETS1-3: Evaluate a solution to a complex real-world problem based on prioritized criteria and trade-offs.

title: Power
blurb: Where does all that electricity come from?

teacher.goal: Planned: electricity supply, the grid and substations, and who pays for new power lines.

title: Water
blurb: Computers get hot. How do you cool them?

teacher.goal: Planned: cooling, water use and a town's water supply.

title: Money and schools
blurb: Taxes, tax breaks and what schools get.

teacher.goal: Planned: property taxes, tax abatements and PILOT payments to schools.
